content.name: Marcus Tran
content.title: Clinical Staff Pharmacist (PGY1 Residency Graduate)
content.summary: Pharm.D. graduate and Ohio-licensed pharmacist who completed an ASHP-accredited PGY1 residency, now working as a clinical staff pharmacist in a 400-bed community hospital. Interested in antimicrobial stewardship, where my residency project cut average IV-to-PO conversion time by 1.4 days.

experience.title: Pharmacy Intern (part-time)
bullets: Filled and checked prescriptions under pharmacist supervision in a store processing about 280 prescriptions a day.
Administered 450+ flu, COVID-19 and shingles vaccines after completing APhA immunization training.
Called prescribers and insurers to resolve prior authorizations, clearing a backlog of 60 pending claims in three weeks.

experience.title: PGY1 Pharmacy Resident
bullets: Rotated through internal medicine, critical care, infectious diseases, oncology and ambulatory care, rounding daily with physician teams.
Led a residency project on IV-to-PO antibiotic conversion that shortened average conversion time from 3.1 to 1.7 days.
Precepted 6 fourth-year Pharm.D. students on APPE rotations and delivered 4 accredited CE presentations to pharmacy staff.
Drafted a vancomycin AUC-based dosing protocol adopted by the pharmacy and therapeutics committee.

experience.title: Clinical Staff Pharmacist
bullets: Verify about 350 inpatient medication orders per shift and manage pharmacy-to-dose consults for vancomycin, aminoglycosides and warfarin.
Respond to codes and rapid responses as the pharmacy representative, preparing emergency medications at the bedside.
Support antimicrobial stewardship rounds twice a week, flagging de-escalation opportunities for the ID physician.

education.school: The Ohio State University College of Pharmacy

achievements.title: Licensed Pharmacist, Ohio State Board of Pharmacy
achievements.detail: Passed NAPLEX and the Ohio MPJE in 2025.

achievements.title: Residency research poster
achievements.detail: Presented the IV-to-PO project at the ASHP Midyear Clinical Meeting, 2025.
